title: OpCraft: StepForge — compact playbook composer for fast incident fixes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
On-call engineers frequently need to cobble together short, safe remediation playbooks (6–10 steps) during incidents. Current runbook creation is heavyweight: PRs, YAML schema authoring, and manual permissions checks. That friction increases time-to-first-fix and discourages capturing small fixes as re-usable playbooks.

Goal:
Build a lightweight composer (StepForge) that lets an authorized operator assemble parameterized 'playlets' (compact, verified runbooks) via a minimal UI or CLI: choose typed inputs, attach pre-built safe actions (e.g., restart, toggle-flag, rollout-rollback), simulate a dry-run, and push either (a) an ephemeral task to the admin quickflow runner or (b) a production runlet artifact (YAML) with an automated PR. The tool should integrate telemetry suggestions to auto-capture key observability queries for each step.

Scope (MVP):
- Web UI for composing 1–10 step playlets with typed inputs and basic validation.
- Dry-run simulator against a sandbox environment (no production side-effects).
- Role-gated execution: only users in 'ops-runlet-auth' can execute non-dry runs.
- Auto-generate YAML spec and optional GitHub PR stub that the infra team can promote.
- Telemetry hints: suggest useful logs/metrics dashboards and attach one synthetic regression test case.

Out of scope (MVP):
- Full policy-based RBAC integration with enterprise SSO (follow-up).
- Complex orchestration flows (waiting, branching) — limited to sequential steps.

Success metrics:
- Time to author and run a 5-step playlet < 8 minutes (authors measured with telemetry).
- 50% reduction in ad-hoc Slack remediation posts converted to playlets within 6 weeks of launch.
- Zero unsafe incidents caused by StepForge in first 3 months (safety-telemetry).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Store ephemeral playlets in central registry vs. ephemeral only on user account — decided to store ephemeral playlets for 30 days with audit logs to allow rerun.
- Simulation fidelity vs. complexity: MVP will mock external system responses and validate API contract shape only.

Rollout plan:
1) Ship internal opt-in beta to SRE and first-oncall rotation.
2) Collect telemetry and safety logs; iterate on forbidden-actions list.
3) 1:1 training sessions with platform support and update docs.

Roll-forward/rollback strategy:
- Feature toggle on console; automatic fallback to legacy runbook creation if simulator or executor returns unexpected error codes.

Notes on safety:
- All non-dry executions require confirmation and a 2-minute safety window where a cancel endpoint can abort execution (implemented by executor).
- Every produced YAML includes an immutable provenance header (author, timestamp, step hashes).
acceptance_criteria: Compose and save a 3-step playlet in the UI with typed inputs and validate the input schema
Run a dry-run and assert no production-side effects in sandbox telemetry
Execute a gated non-dry run with a user in 'ops-runlet-auth' and verify audit entry appears in admin-audit logs
Auto-generate a GitHub PR with the YAML artifact and a one-line description referencing the incident ID
Attach at least one telemetry hint (log query or dashboard link) to the playlet before saving
